description: HTTP + WebSocket layer, auth, input validation, the full REST surface, the WS hub, the index.ts bootstrap, and the integration tests — then the boot-without-PM2 acceptance verification (AC4-AC7). Depends on FEAT-001..003 (state hub, pm2 client, alert engine, channels, config). Grounded in design.md 'HTTP/API layer', 'REST API surface', 'WebSocket layer', 'WebSocket message protocol', 'Authentication', 'Input validation and sanitization', 'Entry point', 'Graceful degradation', and the error-handling table.
steps: src/api/auth.ts: the single length-guarded safeEqual(provided,expected) that sha256-hashes both sides to 32-byte digests then calls timingSafeEqual (never throws, returns false on any mismatch). Express auth middleware: apikey mode checks X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer via safeEqual(provided,API_KEY); basic mode decodes Authorization: Basic and checks user and pass each via safeEqual against BASIC_USER/BASIC_PASS (both must pass), 401 + WWW-Authenticate on mismatch. Export safeEqual for reuse by the WS upgrade handler. Add src/api/auth.test.ts (safeEqual never throws on empty/wrong-length/malformed, true on exact; middleware 401 paths).

src/api/schemas.ts + src/api/validate.ts: validate(schema) middleware parsing {body,query,params} -> 400 {error:{code:'VALIDATION',message}}; process-name rule /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}$/; script-path rule (path.isAbsolute, path.normalize, reject .. segments, allowed extension .js/.cjs/.mjs/.ts/.py/.sh configurable, fs.existsSync, optional ALLOWED_SCRIPT_ROOT prefix); ecosystem-path rule (.js/.cjs/.config.js/.json); create-process body with instances z.number().int().min(1).max(128).optional(), exec_mode z.enum(['fork','cluster']).optional(), XOR script/ecosystem refinement, instances>1 => cluster (reject fork+instances>1; default cluster when instances>1 and no exec_mode); numeric query clamps for lines(<=2000 default 200), limit, sinceMs, durationMin (negatives 400). Add src/api/schemas.test.ts (injection strings rejected, bounds/refinements/XOR/clamps).

src/api/routes/processes.ts: GET /api/processes (auth) ProcessSnapshot[]; GET /api/processes/:name 404 if unknown; GET /api/processes/:name/metrics ?sinceMs (default 1h) via MonitorState.getMetrics; POST start/stop/restart/reload, DELETE :name, POST /api/processes (startNew, 201) each returning ControlResult with 409 PM2_UNAVAILABLE when disconnected and 502 PM2_ERROR on pm2-side failure; GET /api/processes/:name/logs resolving :name against the snapshot map FIRST (404 unknown) then readLogsTail (200 {lines:[]} only when known-but-file-missing), supporting ?lines ?stream ?q ?level.

src/api/routes/logs.ts, src/api/routes/errors.ts (GET /api/errors list + GET /api/errors/export json|csv with Content-Disposition attachment), src/api/routes/alerts.ts (GET /api/alerts/rules secrets-free, POST /api/alerts/rules/reload re-running loadAlertRules + engine.reload (400 with issues on invalid), POST /api/alerts/test, GET /api/alerts/recent, GET+POST /api/maintenance). All auth-gated except health.

src/api/server.ts: createServer(deps): http.Server — express.json({limit:'64kb'}), a request logger using redactUrl, auth middleware wiring, route mounts under /api, express.static('public') at /, a terminal error handler mapping thrown/next errors to {error:{code,message}} with status codes (200/201/400 VALIDATION/401 UNAUTHORIZED/404 NOT_FOUND/409 PM2_UNAVAILABLE/502 PM2_ERROR/500), 5xx logged error, 4xx debug. Return the shared http.Server (not app.listen) so the WS hub attaches to the same server.

src/ws/hub.ts: WsHub attaching a ws WebSocketServer in noServer mode to the shared server; handle 'upgrade' for /ws: extract credential from the offered apikey.<KEY> subprotocol or ?token= param, validate with the SAME safeEqual; on success handleUpgrade echoing the exact offered subprotocol as accepted; on failure write HTTP/1.1 401 and destroy the socket before handshake. NEVER log req.url on the upgrade path — only the fixed '/ws' plus an authed boolean. Per-client subscription sets; handle client messages subscribe/log:subscribe/log:unsubscribe/ping; send hello (with snapshot) on connect, state (throttled/coalesced to <=1/sec), process:transition, log (per-process fan-out off log:line to subscribers only), alert, pm2, pong, error BAD_MESSAGE. Subscribe to the state hub + alert events.
src/testutil/fakePm2Client.ts: a fake implementing the Pm2Client interface with configurable connected flag and canned snapshots/control results for integration tests.

src/api/server.test.ts + src/ws/hub.test.ts: node:test integration using Node's http + ws clients against the real app with the fake Pm2Client — assert auth 401, validation 400, control happy/error, 409 when disconnected, graceful-degradation (pm2Connected:false still serves / and health), and WS hello/subscription-filtering/log-fan-out/upgrade-auth-rejection without crashing.

src/index.ts: full bootstrap in order — loadConfig -> build logger -> loadAlertRules -> construct MonitorState/MetricsStore/ErrorTracker -> construct channels -> construct AlertEngine and wire events (ensure MonitorState subscribes to metrics:tick before AlertEngine) -> construct Pm2Client and call start() (non-blocking; HTTP must come up even if PM2 is down) -> createServer + WsHub -> server.listen(PORT,HOST) -> start digest scheduler. SIGINT/SIGTERM graceful shutdown (stop accepting, close WS, pm2Client.stop(), flush error log, exit 0); unhandledRejection/uncaughtException logged, uncaught -> graceful shutdown exit 1.

Boot-without-PM2 acceptance (AC4-AC7): with no pm2 daemon running, npm run build then node dist/index.js with a minimal apikey-mode .env (set API_KEY and a PORT); confirm the process stays up, logs a reconnect warning, GET / returns dashboard HTML (serve the placeholder public/index.html if FEAT-005 not yet done, or confirm static mount returns something), and GET /api/system/health returns JSON with pm2Connected:false; then stop the process. Record the outcome in findings.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build compiles with ZERO TypeScript errors.
npm test passes including the API and WS integration tests.
safeEqual is the only credential comparison and is used by both REST auth and the WS upgrade; a wrong-length WS credential returns 401 without crashing the process.

With PM2 not running the app boots, GET / returns HTML, GET /api/system/health returns JSON with pm2Connected:false, control endpoints return 409 PM2_UNAVAILABLE, and the process does not crash (AC4-AC7, AC15).
Every /api/* endpoint requires auth except GET /api/system/health; unauthenticated requests to protected endpoints get 401.
verification: Run: npm run build  — zero tsc strict errors.
Run: npm test  — all unit + integration tests pass.

Boot check: node dist/index.js with pm2 absent and a minimal apikey .env; curl -s localhost:$PORT/ returns HTML and curl -s localhost:$PORT/api/system/health returns JSON pm2Connected:false; process stays up; stop it afterward.
findings:
VERIFIED: npm run build => 0 tsc strict errors; npm test => 156 pass / 0 fail (117 FEAT-001..003 + 39 new: auth 11, schemas 9, server 13, ws/hub 6). PM2 daemon NOT running before/after (pgrep + ~/.pm2 removed). Boot-without-PM2 (AC4-AC7) PASSED and the spawned-daemon trap was found and fixed (see DAEMON FIX).

BOOT CHECK (AC4-AC7, AC15): built, wrote a temp apikey .env (API_KEY + PORT=38217, HOST=127.0.0.1), ran `node dist/index.js`. Result: process stays up; logs warn 'pm2 connect failed; starting reconnect loop'; GET / => 200 dashboard HTML (placeholder public/index.html, see below); GET /api/system/health => 200 {status:'ok',pm2Connected:false,maintenance:false,uptimeMs,version:'1.0.0'}; POST /api/processes/<n>/restart (authed) => 409 {error.code:'PM2_UNAVAILABLE'}. SIGTERM => clean graceful shutdown ('shutting down' log, server stops). .env deleted afterward (never committed); ~/.pm2 removed; NO PM2 daemon left running.

DAEMON FIX (confined to the single pm2 import site, src/pm2/client.ts createPm2Adapter.connect; FEAT-002 client logic + its 14 tests untouched and still green): pm2.connect() LAUNCHES a God Daemon when none is running (daemon mode default) — the first boot attempt actually spawned ~/.pm2 God Daemon and health reported pm2Connected:true, violating both AC4-AC7 and the hard 'PM2 must NOT be started' constraint. Fix: gate connect on pm2.Client.pingDaemon(cb) — attach only if a daemon is already alive, else callback an Error('PM2 daemon is not running') so the existing Pm2Client reconnect loop keeps pm2Connected=false and retries. This never launches a daemon and is faithful to the design 'Graceful degradation' contract (connect is recoverable/background-retry when the daemon is down). Behavior when a daemon IS running is unchanged (still attaches). Later features that exercise real control must have an operator-started daemon; the monitor itself will never start one.

PLACEHOLDER public/index.html: FEAT-005 owns the real dashboard; FEAT-004 added a minimal public/index.html so the express.static mount serves HTML for the boot check. FEAT-005 should REPLACE it (and add css/ + js/). The static root is resolved as path.resolve(__dirname,'..','public') from dist/ (i.e. project-root/public), so built code finds it.

NEW FILES: src/api/auth.ts (+auth.test.ts), src/api/schemas.ts (+schemas.test.ts), src/api/validate.ts, src/api/server.ts (+server.test.ts), src/api/routes/{system,processes,logs,errors,alerts}.ts, src/ws/hub.ts (+hub.test.ts), src/testutil/fakePm2Client.ts, public/index.html. MODIFIED: src/index.ts (stub -> full bootstrap), src/pm2/client.ts (daemon-fix only).

AUTH (src/api/auth.ts): safeEqual(provided,expected) sha256->32-byte digests->timingSafeEqual, never throws, returns false on any mismatch — the ONLY credential comparison, reused by REST createAuthMiddleware (apikey: X-API-Key or Authorization:Bearer; basic: decode Authorization:Basic, user AND pass each via safeEqual, 401+WWW-Authenticate) AND by WS validateWsCredential (apikey: raw key; basic: base64 user:pass). apiError(status,code,message) helper for thrown route errors. auth.test.ts asserts safeEqual never throws on empty/wrong-length/malformed/undefined and is true only on exact match, plus the middleware 401 paths.

VALIDATION (src/api/validate.ts + schemas.ts): validate(schema) parses {body,query,params} and stores the parsed/coerced result in res.locals.validated (read via validated<T>(res)); on zod failure => 400 {error:{code:'VALIDATION',message}} (issues summarized). buildSchemas(opts:{allowedScriptRoot?,scriptExts?,fileExists?}) returns the schema bag; process-name /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}$/; script-path (isAbsolute, normalize, reject '..' segments, ext in .js/.cjs/.mjs/.ts/.py/.sh, fileExists, optional ALLOWED_SCRIPT_ROOT prefix); ecosystem-path (.js/.cjs/.config.js/.json); create-process body strict with instances 1..128, exec_mode fork|cluster, XOR script/ecosystem refinement, reject fork+instances>1, default cluster when instances>1 & no exec_mode; numeric query clamps lines(<=2000 default 200), limit(<=1000), recent limit(<=200), sinceMs(default 1h for metrics), negatives=>400. schemas.test.ts covers injection rejection, XOR, bounds, cluster refinement, ALLOWED_SCRIPT_ROOT, and clamps (fileExists injected).

SERVER (src/api/server.ts): createServer(deps:ApiDeps):http.Server — express.json({limit:'64kb'}), redacting request logger (redactUrl), health router mounted on /api/system BEFORE auth (the single UNAUTH /api endpoint), auth applied to /api, then /api/system(status)/processes/errors/alerts/maintenance routers, express.static(publicDir) at /, an /api 404, and a terminal error handler mapping to {error:{code,message}} (5xx logged error w/ redacted url+stack, 4xx debug). Returns the shared http.Server (NOT app.listen) so WsHub attaches to the same port. ApiDeps exposes narrow surfaces (StateDeps/Pm2Deps/EngineDeps/ErrorsDeps) + schemas, auth, logger, publicDir, version, startedAt, now, getRules/setRules, reloadRules(): {ok:true,rules}|{ok:false,message} (NEVER exits — runtime reload uses alertRulesFileSchema.safeParse, distinct from loadAlertRules which exits). ControlResult mapping: ok=>200 (201 for POST /api/processes create), PM2_UNAVAILABLE=>409, any other not-ok=>502. /api/processes/:name/logs resolves :name against the snapshot FIRST (404 unknown) then readLogsTail (200 {name,lines:[]} when known-but-file-missing).

WS HUB (src/ws/hub.ts): WsHub({server,events,auth,logger,snapshot,now?,setTimer?,clearTimer?}) attaches a ws WebSocketServer in noServer mode; handles 'upgrade' for /ws only; extracts credential from offered apikey.<KEY> subprotocol or ?token=; validates via the SAME validateWsCredential/safeEqual; on fail writes 'HTTP/1.1 401' + destroys socket (no WebSocket constructed); on success handleUpgrade with the WebSocketServer handleProtocols callback echoing the exact apikey.* subprotocol back (compliant browsers require the echo). NEVER logs req.url on upgrade — only {path:'/ws',authed}. Per-client channels Set + per-process logSubs Map<name,Set<stream>>; client msgs subscribe/log:subscribe/log:unsubscribe/ping; server msgs hello(on connect, with snapshot+serverTime), state (coalesced to <=1/sec via a throttle timer), process:transition, log (per-process+stream fan-out off log:line), alert, pm2(connected), pong, error BAD_MESSAGE. close() detaches all listeners, cancels the throttle timer, closes clients + wss. hub.test.ts (node http + ws clients): authed upgrade+hello, wrong-length cred => 401 via 'unexpected-response' (NOT 'error'; process survives, a fresh authed connect succeeds), ?token= fallback, state subscription filtering, log fan-out filtering, ping/pong + BAD_MESSAGE.
  WS TEST GOTCHAS (for later WS test authors): (1) a 401-rejected upgrade makes the ws client emit 'unexpected-response' (res.statusCode 401) and NO 'error'/'close' — awaiting 'error' hangs forever; listen for 'unexpected-response'. (2) hello is pushed immediately on connect, so a reader that attaches a 'message' listener AFTER awaiting 'open' can miss it; the test uses a MessageQueue that buffers from socket construction.

BOOTSTRAP (src/index.ts): bootstrap() in design order — loadConfig -> createLogger(level) -> loadAlertRules -> MonitorEvents -> MetricsStore -> ErrorTracker -> MonitorState (constructed BEFORE AlertEngine so it subscribes to metrics:tick first) -> TeamsChannel + EmailChannel(await verify()) -> AlertEngine (with an AlertStateHub ADAPTER: processNames()=snapshot().processes.map(name), sustainedAbove delegates to the hub-owned MetricsStore — not reached directly) -> Pm2Client.start() (non-blocking) -> createServer + WsHub -> server.listen -> DigestScheduler.start(). Digest AlertCounters are fed by tallying 'alert' events (delivered=>dispatched, else=>suppressed) — an approximation (cooldown-suppressed matches are not emitted, as FEAT-003 noted). reloadRules reads ALERT_RULES_FILE + safeParse (no exit). Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM (wsHub.close, digest.stop, server.close, pm2.stop, state/errors/engine.stop, exit 0); unhandledRejection logged; uncaughtException logged + graceful shutdown exit 1. The file self-boots only when run directly (argv[1] === this module), so test imports never boot.

FAKE (src/testutil/fakePm2Client.ts): FakePm2Client implements the Pm2Client public surface (isConnected/start/stop/list/describe/control/startNew/readLogsTail) with configurable connected flag, canned processes/controlResult/startNewResult/logs, and records controlCalls/startNewCalls. makeSnapshot(partial) builds a ProcessSnapshot. Used by server.test.ts (and available to future WS/integration tests).

NODE-TEST CAVEAT reconfirmed: integration tests use Node's own http + ws clients (no supertest), per-test servers on port 0, and must settle every socket/promise or the whole FILE reports as one cancelled test (the test runner aggregates a hung subtest at file level with no per-subtest output).
